event: Advance notice of proposed rulemaking after Seminole Tribe of Florida v. Florida, 116 S. Ct. 1114 (1996), asking for comment on Interior's authority to prescribe class III procedures when a State pleads immunity.
Correction of the issuing agency and CFR part number on the 1996 notice.
Proposed rule (Interior concluded it has authority to prescribe procedures when a State asserts immunity).
Comment period on the proposed rule extended.
Final rule creating 25 C.F.R. part 291; regulation text at 64 Fed. Reg. 17543; effective May 12, 1999 (per earlier research).

Fifth Circuit holds the Secretary lacked authority to promulgate part 291 (Texas v. United States, Kickapoo Traditional Tribe of Texas intervening; opinion revised Sept. 13, 2007; one judge dissenting).
citation: Texas v. United States, 497 F.3d 491 (5th Cir. 2007)

event: Tenth Circuit affirms: part 291 is not a valid exercise of the Secretary's authority, as it is foreclosed by IGRA's text (arising from the Pueblo of Pojoaque request).
citation: New Mexico v. Dep't of the Interior, Nos. 14-2219 & 14-2222 (10th Cir. 2017)

event: Interior's revision of 25 C.F.R. part 293 (compact review). Not an amendment of part 291; cited because Interior's 2025 Rincon letter mentions the part 293 changes.
Paperwork Reduction Act renewal notice covering information collections in 25 C.F.R. 290-293 (shows part 291 still carries an OMB collection).

§ 291.1 Purpose and scope: Says the part sets the process the Secretary uses to prescribe class III gaming rules when a State and a tribe cannot agree on a compact and the State has asserted immunity from the tribe's suit under 2710(d)(7)(B).
§ 291.2 Definitions: IGRA definitions apply; 'compact' includes renewal of an existing compact.

§ 291.3 When may an Indian tribe ask the Secretary to issue Class III gaming procedures?: Five preconditions: written request to negotiate; no compact 180 days later; suit in federal court alleging no or bad-faith response; State raised an Eleventh Amendment defense; court dismissed on that ground.

§ 291.4 What must a proposal requesting Class III gaming procedures contain?: Tribe's identifying data and authorizing resolution, gaming ordinance, organic documents, negotiation correspondence, the litigation papers, legal authority for the games, State oversight scheme, and proposed procedures covering 19 items (accounting, internal controls, records, conduct of games, licensing, health and safety, surveillance, an administrative or tribal-court process for disputes among the operation, employees and patrons, enforcement and sanctions, duration, other).
§ 291.5 Where must the proposal be filed?: With the Director, Indian Gaming Management Staff, BIA, Washington, DC.

§ 291.6 What must the Secretary do upon receiving a proposal?: Within 15 days notify the tribe of receipt and missing items; within 30 days of a complete proposal notify the tribe whether it meets 291.3. That eligibility decision is final for the Department.

§ 291.7 What must the Secretary do if the tribe is eligible?: Send the proposal to the Governor and Attorney General, who have 60 days to comment (agreement, consistency with state law, whether the games are permitted in the State) and are invited to submit an alternative proposal.

§ 291.8 What must the Secretary do if the State has not submitted an alternative proposal?: Review the proposal against seven criteria (291.4 completeness, Indian lands jurisdiction, games permitted in the State, state law, trust obligations, IGRA, other federal law). Within 60 days approve it, or identify unresolved issues and invite an informal conference within 30 days; within 30 days of that conference issue a written report and a final decision setting the Secretary's procedures or disapproving.

§ 291.9 What must the Secretary do if the State offers an alternative proposal?: Within 30 days of the State's proposal, appoint a mediator with no conflict of interest to convene a process to resolve the differences.

§ 291.10 What is the role of the mediator appointed by the Secretary?: Ask for each side's last best proposal, hear both, select the one that best comports with IGRA and other federal law, and submit it to the tribe, the State and the Secretary.

§ 291.11 What must the Secretary do upon receiving the mediator's proposal?: Within 60 days approve it, or disapprove it on the seven grounds; if disapproved, prescribe within 60 days procedures that follow the mediator's selection as much as possible, IGRA and state law.
§ 291.12 Who will monitor and enforce tribal compliance?: The tribe and State may agree on monitoring and enforcement; the NIGC monitors and enforces under existing law.

§ 291.13 When do the procedures become effective?: After approval the tribe has 90 days to approve and execute them and return them; the Secretary publishes notice of approval in the Federal Register and the procedures take effect on that publication.

§ 291.14 How can approved procedures be amended?: The tribe submits an amendment proposal; the Secretary follows the same approval process, except 291.3 does not apply and 291.4 may be waived to the extent inapplicable.
§ 291.15 How long do the procedures remain in effect?: For the duration stated in the procedures or until amended under 291.14.
